## How the score was worked out

Each result implies a score on its own, after adjusting for how hard that test is and who ran it. The model's score is their weighted average, with a small pull toward the middle for thinly tested models. Each test's weight is its *counts* column above; here it is added up by who ran the tests. [Method](../method.md)

## How to run it

### Other ways to run it

1. Run it as published (BF16, needs ~8.29 GB, NVIDIA only, from [github.com/vllm-project](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/64cb68384241f046d07ba3797e1b14dbc82a0b2d/docs/models/supported_models.md))
   
   ```sh
   vllm serve microsoft/Phi-3-vision-128k-instruct --trust-remote-code
   ```

Official weights and documentation: [huggingface.co/microsoft](https://huggingface.co/microsoft/Phi-3-vision-128k-instruct)
